title.narrative: Number of individuals directly benefitting from EU supported actions that specifically aim to support civilian post conflict peacebuilding and/or conflict prevention

description.narrative: Number of individuals directly benefitting from EU supported actions that specifically aim to support civilian post conflict peacebuilding and/or conflict prevention

comment.narrative: A total of 1 571 256 individuals directly benefitted from the action as follows 20 community influencers 5 women and 15 men who participated in the PVE training workshops 1 570 735 community members who took part in the screening sessions of the community stories videos 528 women and 309 men in the live airing sessions of the radio drama 157 women and 144 men in the subgrantee projects 232 women and girls and 211 men and boys in the youth interfaith exhibitions 2700 visitors who listened to the radio drama 1 564 900 listeners per episode on average and who watched the community stories videos on YouTube 224 people and on X 1330 people. 20 media professionals 6 women and 14 men who were trained in PVE 221 Salafi community members who took part in the PCVE training for atrisk women and youth 86 women and 34 men from the Salafi community and in the local dialogues with local government representatives 31 women and 70 men from the Salafi community. 68 representatives of government institutions governance and security agencies at local and national levels who participated in the 2nd knowledge exchange workshop on reintegration of former fighters one woman and 5 men in local dialogues with Salafi community 5 women and 21 men in the Kampala lessons learnt conference 4 women and 10 men and in the village dialogues with exmembers of the ADF called returnees 6 women and 16 men. 28 civil society leaders 14 women and 14 men who participated in PVE training workshops. 164 returnees or former members of the ADF 69 women and 95 men who participated in video interviews for the community stories in CVE training workshops in the exchange visit to Gulu to meet with former members of the LRA who have successfully reintegrated into society and in the village dialogues with local government representatives.

title.narrative: Number of people arrested for terrorist related offences

description.narrative: Number of people arrested for terrorist related offences

comment.narrative: Project indicator Number of violent extremist attacks and arrests of suspected members of terror cells reported in project localities. Target By 2024 a decrease in the number of violent extremist attacks and arrests reported in project localities compared to baseline data.

The project did not achieve the expected impact when it comes to contributing to reducing the number of violent extremism VE incidents. In fact according to the 2023 Police Annual Crime Report 26 terrorism cases were reported in 2023 vs 15 cases in 2022. In the absence of available data for 2024 it is premature to assess the full impact of the project on the number of VE incidents. But this uptick in the 2023 number of cases can also demonstrate increased vigilance of the local population following the projects awareness raising trust building and capacity building activities which ultimately contributed to an increase in the reporting of terrorist incidents. This is correlated by testimonies from local security authorities who report an increase in the information they receive from local communities including returnees with whom relationships were difficult before the project as well as an increase in communities vigilance.

comment.narrative: The intervention was designed in 2022 as a response to the quickly deteriorating security situation due to violent extremism in Uganda. After a lull with no terror attack since 2015 Uganda registered the largest deterioration in the Global Terrorism Index score in 2021. This recent deterioration is due to the increased frequency boldness sophistication and complexity of terrorist activities by the Allied Democratic Forces including its most dramatic attacks perpetrated in Kampala in August and November 2021 and in Kasese school in June 2023.
